confirmed.title: Sliding-window filter is inverted: it keeps expired events and drops in-window ones, so the limiter never limits
confirmed.evidence: `if t.Before(cutoff) { kept = append(kept, t) }` keeps only events older than now-Window; New(2, time.Minute) allows 10 of 10 calls at the same instant.
confirmed.reproduction: Scratch copy + in-package test with fixed clock: New(2, time.Minute), 10x Allow("a") -> 'same-instant allowed=10 of 10 (limit 2)'.

confirmed.title: drain() uses forEach(async) and returns before any job finishes, so it always returns 0
confirmed.evidence: `batch.forEach(async (job) => { if (await this.runOne(job)) ok += 1; }); return ok;` forEach discards the promises; drain resolves to 0 and async jobs complete afterwards.
confirmed.fix_hint: `for (const job of batch) { if (await this.runOne(job)) ok += 1; }`
confirmed.reproduction: 3 async jobs (10ms): `await q.drain()` -> 0, completed 0; after 50ms completed 3. Sync jobs: drain still returns 0.

confirmed.title: Mutable default `tags=[]` is shared and mutated, so tags leak between items
confirmed.evidence: `def add(..., tags=[])` then `tags.append("new")`; every add() without tags shares one list, across Inventory instances, and caller lists are mutated.
confirmed.reproduction: inv.add('a',...), inv.add('b',...) -> ['new','new'] ['new','new'] True; fresh Inventory add -> ['new','new','new']; caller list ['x'] -> ['x','new'].
